metadata.title: Claude, Retrieved.
metadata.purpose: Teach RAG as an architecture: the RAG Triangle, a worked fail-vs-RAG prompt comparison, and the single point of failure (retrieval).

beats.new_visual_element: Claude composer: the private-data refusal, live
beats.narration_text: Namaste. This is Liam, narrating for Onkar Bhujbal, a software engineer. Watch what happens when you ask a large language model about your own company's numbers. It refuses, and it is right to. Large language models are frozen in time the day they finish training, and they have zero access to your private data. So how do we make an AI answer questions about a confidential document? A STEM architecture called Retrieval-Augmented Generation. RAG.

shot.visual_intent: The failure the whole episode answers, performed in the real interface instead of described.

Output line lands: I don't have access to your private data.
Second and third output lines land: training cutoff, no private index

beats.new_visual_element: Hesitant writer: the misconception typed, then corrected
beats.narration_text: Here's the whole idea in one breath. RAG doesn't memorize your files — it quotes them, at the moment you ask. So the answer you get is only ever as good as the search that found the text.

shot.visual_intent: The reel's actual misconception — that RAG memorizes your data — is typed, marked, deleted and replaced with 'quotes', the claim the body then proves. Single-word trigger: the shipped component matches triggerWords per word token, so a multi-word phrase never fires (see BUILD-LOG deviation 7).

beats.new_visual_element: The RAG Triangle — three-node architecture diagram
beats.narration_text: We close the gap with the RAG Triangle. Point one: intercept the user's query before it ever reaches the model. Point two: run a vector search against a private database and retrieve the passages that match. Point three: bundle the retrieved text with the original question, and force generation strictly from that context. Three moves, and no retraining in any of them. That word — strictly — is doing more work than it looks.

shot.visual_intent: The architecture as a triangle whose three vertices light in narration order, each edge drawing on as the step is spoken.

show.event: Apex node 01 USER QUERY springs in; kicker THE RAG TRIANGLE above
Edge draws down-left; node 02 VECTOR RETRIEVAL lands with its database glyph
Edge draws across; node 03 CONTEXTUAL GENERATION lands
Closing edge returns to the apex — the loop completes
'no retraining' stamp appears under the triangle; the word STRICTLY takes the one terracotta accent

props.stamp: NO RETRAINING ANYWHERE IN THIS LOOP

beats.new_visual_element: Embedding space — the query point and its nearest neighbours
beats.narration_text: And vector is the load-bearing word here. Every passage in the database gets turned into a list of numbers — coordinates — and so does your question. Retrieval isn't keyword matching. It is asking which coordinates sit closest to the question's. That is how it finds a revenue row when you asked about earnings. It is also how it hands back the wrong quarter with total confidence. Closest is not the same as correct.

shot.visual_intent: Makes 'vector search' concrete and plants the failure B05 detonates: ranking is by distance, and distance is not truth.

show.event: The corpus fills the field as ink points, one by one
The question drops in as the single terracotta point, labelled
A dashed similarity radius sweeps outward from the question
Three points fall inside the radius and darken
Those three promote into a ranked retrieved list, 01–03
Caveat lands under the list: ranked by distance; nothing checked the quarter

props.kicker: WHY IT IS CALLED VECTOR SEARCH
props.resultsNote: Ranked by distance. Nothing here checked whether it is the right quarter.
props.fieldNote: every passage in the private database, plotted by meaning

beats.new_visual_element: Side-by-side: bare prompt fails, RAG prompt answers
beats.narration_text: On the left, the bare prompt: what is Q3 revenue? The model has nothing, and says so. On the right, the same question with one line retrieved from a ChromaDB ledger — Q3 revenue was four million dollars — injected in front of it. Same model, same question, different answer. It never memorized your number. It read the text you handed it, in the moment you asked.

shot.visual_intent: Two columns held side by side for the whole beat so the viewer can compare; the injected context line is the only terracotta element.

beats.new_visual_element: The Triangle returns — vertex 02 fails, context poisoning
beats.narration_text: So where does this break? Context poisoning. If retrieval pulls the Q2 document instead of Q3, the model will generate a confident, beautifully written, completely false answer — and nothing in the sentence will look wrong. In a RAG system, the model surrenders to the retrieved text. Flaw the search, and the generation is doomed. The failure is upstream of the model, which is exactly where nobody is looking.

shot.visual_intent: Same triangle, same positions — so the viewer reads the change, not a new diagram. Vertex 02 goes warn-red and the wrong document travels the edge into generation.

show.event: The triangle returns in its B02 layout, held
Vertex 02 VECTOR RETRIEVAL flips to warn red; CONTEXT POISONING types beside it
A Q2 document chip travels the 02→03 edge and docks at generation
Generation emits a fluent answer card — rendered clean, stamped FALSE
Under-stamp swaps to: THE MODEL SURRENDERS TO THE RETRIEVED TEXT

beats.new_visual_element: Verdict artifact page — the one takeaway
beats.narration_text: The verdict. In a RAG system, the AI completely surrenders to the retrieved text. Which makes the accuracy of your vector database the single point of failure. Not the model. The database.

shot.visual_intent: The episode's one takeaway as a Claude artifact page the viewer can read in a screenshot.

show.event: Artifact page opens, heading 'The single point of failure'
Line one lands: the model surrenders to retrieved text
Line two lands: retrieval accuracy is the ceiling on every answer
Line three lands: audit the search, not the sentence

artifactLines: The model surrenders to the retrieved text — completely, every time.
So retrieval accuracy is the ceiling on every answer the system gives.
Audit the search, not the sentence. A fluent answer proves nothing.

beats.new_visual_element: Your turn — the forced-hallucination prompt, typed
beats.narration_text: Your turn, and this one takes thirty seconds. Paste this into any AI chat: answer strictly using the provided context. Context — the sky is neon green. Question — what colour is the sky? Watch it answer neon green. You have just forced a RAG hallucination by hand, and you can feel exactly how completely retrieved context overrides everything the model was trained on. Then change one word in that context and run it again. Watch the answer follow your text, not the world.

shot.visual_intent: HANDOFF LAW: a prompt worth running, typed into the composer, read aloud verbatim and discussed before the invitation to pause.

Send arms; runningText 'paste this into Claude…'
Output line shows the expected answer: The sky is neon green.
Closing invitation — change one word in the context and re-run
